chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us, he said: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id reported to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Marwan reported to us, he said: my father reported to me, he said: Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam reported to us, from al-Mas'udi, he said: al-Harith ibn Hasirah reported to us, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said:

I and Umar ibn al-Khattab were sitting with the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, and Ali, peace be upon him, was sitting by his side, when the Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, recited:
"Or who answers the distressed when he calls upon Him and relieves the affliction, and makes you successors on the earth? Is there a god with God? Little do you reflect."

He said: Ali, peace be upon him, quivered like a bird. The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said to him: "What is the matter with you that you are so anxious?" He replied: "Why would I not be anxious when God says He will make us successors on the earth!" The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, said to him: "Do not be anxious, for by God, none shall love you except a believer, and none shall hate you except a hypocrite."

key_terms.المضطر: The distressed one, the one in dire need who calls upon God
key_terms.انتفاضة العصفور: Quivering like a bird -- a vivid metaphor for trembling with awe or concern
key_terms.خلفاء الأرض: Successors on the earth, vicegerents -- referring to divine appointment of righteous leaders
key_terms.مؤمن: Believer, one who has genuine faith
key_terms.منافق: Hypocrite, one who outwardly professes faith while inwardly concealing disbelief

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about loving and hating Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: This narration records an incident where the Prophet (SAWW) recited Quran 27:62 about God's promise to make righteous people successors on earth. Ali (AS), sitting beside the Prophet, quivered with awe at the weight of this divine promise. The Prophet reassured him with the famous declaration that love for Ali is the mark of a true believer, while hatred for him is the sign of hypocrisy -- a statement transmitted through multiple early Islamic sources and considered among the well-known virtues of Ali in Shia tradition.
